title: m6A-label-seq: A metabolic labeling protocol to detect transcriptome-wide mRNA N6-methyladenosine (m6A) at base resolution
protocol: Dissolve Se-allyl-L-selenohomocysteine in sterile water to a final concentration of 50 mM.
Dissolve L-cysteine in sterile water to a final concentration of 100 mM.
Prepare methionine-deficient medium by supplementing RPMI 1640 (methionine-deficient) with 10% FBS, 1% Penicillin/Streptomycin Solution and L-cysteine at a final concentration of 1 mM.
Add Se-allyl-L-selenohomocysteine to the methionine-deficient medium to achieve a final concentration of 1 mM for feeding medium preparation.
Remove regular culture medium from cells, wash once with PBS, remove the PBS and then add equal volume of pretreating medium for 30 min incubation at 37°C.
Remove pretreating medium and add equal volume of feeding medium. Culture cells further at 37°C for another 16 h.
After metabolic labeling for 16 h, remove feeding medium from cells.
Wash cells once with cold PBS, remove the PBS.
Add 5 mL TRIzol reagent to 150 mm culture dish to lyse the cells.
Incubate homogenized cell lysate of TRIzol at 20°C–30°C for 5 min.
Transfer mixture to a 15 mL centrifuge tube.
Add 1 mL chloroform (1:5 volume ratio relative to TRIzol) to the tube.
Shake the tube vigorously for 15 s and incubate the mixture for 3 min at 20°C–30°C.
Centrifuge the mixture at 12,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase containing RNA into a new tube by angling the tube at 45° and pipetting carefully.
Add an equal volume of isopropanol to the aqueous solution and mix thoroughly.
Incubate the mixture on ice for 15 minutes.
Centrifuge the mixture at 15,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C to obtain the total RNA precipitate.
Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Wash the pellet once with 6 mL of ice-cold 75% ethanol and centrifuge at 15,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant after washing.
Air dry the RNA pellet at 20-30°C for 5 minutes.
Dissolve the total RNA pellet in 260 μL of RNase-free water and incubate at 60°C for 10 minutes.
Preheat the Elution Solution at 70°C in a heating block.
Pipette 250 μL of total RNA (200-300 μg) into an RNase-free 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 250 μL of 2× Binding Solution to the total RNA and vortex briefly to mix.
Add 20 μL of oligo(dT) beads and vortex thoroughly to mix the contents.
Incubate the mixture at 70°C for 3 min in a heating block.
Remove the sample from the heating block and allow it to stand at 20°C–30°C for 10 min.
Spin at 16,000×g for 2 min at 20°C–30°C.
Carefully remove the supernatant, leaving approximately 50 μL to avoid disturbing the white pellet containing oligo(dT) beads/mRNA complex.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL Wash Solution and mix with a pipette.
Pipet all of the suspension into a GenElute spin filter/collection tube assembly.
Spin at 16,000×g for 2 min at 20°C–30°C and discard the flow-through.
Pipet 500 μL Wash Solution onto the spin filter and spin at 16,000×g for 2 min at 20°C–30°C.
Discard the flow-through and the original collection tube.
Transfer the spin filter into a fresh collection tube.
Add 50 μL Elution Solution (70°C) into the center of the spin filter and incubate for 5 min at 70°C.
Spin at 16,000×g for 2 min at 20°C–30°C and transfer the flow-through into a new 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube to collect polyadenylated RNA.
Add another 30 μL Elution Solution (70°C) into the center of the spin filter and incubate for 5 min at 70°C.
Spin at 16,000×g for 2 min at 20°C–30°C.
Transfer the flow-through into the same 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Transfer 200 μL mRNA products into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 20 μL of 3 M sodium acetate solution (pH = 5.2) to the tube.
Add 220 μL of isopropanol and no more than 2 μL glycogen to the mixture.
Mix the contents thoroughly and incubate at -20°C for about 12–16 hours for precipitation.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Discard supernatant but avoid disturbing the mRNA pellet.
Wash once with 440 μL of 80% ethanol.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Air dry the mRNA pellet for 5 min at 20°C–30°C.
Dissolve mRNA with 36 μL RNase-free water to recover mRNA at a concentration of around 550 ng/μL.
Adjust the concentration of mRNA by adding RNase-free water if needed to be around 500–600 ng/μL.
Add 4 μL 10 × fragmentation buffer to the mRNA solution and mix well.
Incubate at 70°C for 7 min.
Add 8 μL 0.5 M EDTA solution (pH = 8.0) to stop the reaction.
Adjust the volume of mixture into 100 μL by RNase-free water.
Add 1/10 volume (10 μL) of 3 M sodium acetate solution (pH = 5.2).
Add equal volume (110 μL) of isopropanol and no more than 1 μL glycogen.
Mix well and incubate for precipitation about 12–16 h at −20°C.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g for 45 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant but not disturb the mRNA pellet.
Wash once with 220 μL 80% ethanol and centrifuge at 16,000×g for 15 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant again.
Air dry the mRNA pellet for 5 min at 20°C–30°C.
Dissolve mRNA pellet with 100 μL RNase-free water.
Take out about 100 ng mRNA fragments to save as input for library construction at −80°C for one week.
Use the remaining mRNA fragments for immunoprecipitation immediately or store at −80°C for no longer than one week.
Prepare 1.5 mL low-binding microcentrifuge tube, and transfer 5 μg mRNA fragments into it.
Prepare 5× IP buffer freshly before experiment and keep it on ice.
Mix the listed reagents as indicated below.
Incubate with head-over-tail rotation (10 rpm, crystalindustries TR-02U model) for 4 h at 4°C.
Prepare another 1.5 mL low-binding microcentrifuge tube for ProteinA beads incubation.
Prepare 1× IP buffer just before use.
Keep the IP buffer on ice.
Transfer 40 μL ProteinA beads (Dynabeads™ Protein A for Immunoprecipitation) into the tube.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack to separate beads from the supernatant.
After the supernatant becomes clear, carefully remove and discard it.
Resuspend the beads in 200 μL 1× IP buffer.
Pipette to mix and wash.
Place the tube on a magnetic rack to separate beads from the supernatant.
Wait until the supernatant becomes clear (about 2 min).
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the wash step two more times.
Take off the tube for antibody-RNA incubation.
Spin down gently.
Transfer all the solution into the tube containing ProteinA beads.
Resuspend the beads.
Pipette to mix.
Incubate with head-over-tail rotation for 2 hours at 4°C.
Prepare IP wash solution freshly just before use and keep it on ice.
When the incubation of antibody-RNA and proteinA beads is finished, spin down the mixture gently.
Place the mixture on a magnetic rack to separate beads from the supernatant.
Carefully remove and discard the supernatant after the supernatant is clear (about 2 minutes later).
Add 400 μL IP wash solution to immerse the beads.
Wait for 30 seconds and discard the supernatant.
Repeat the wash step once.
Resuspend proteinA beads bound with antibody-RNA complex in 100 μL a6A elution buffer.
Incubate by head-over-tail rotation (10 rpm) with occasional shaking for 3 hours at 4°C.
Spin down the tube gently and place it on a magnetic rack to separate beads from the supernatant.
Wait until the supernatant becomes clear, approximately 2 minutes later at 20°C–30°C.
Carefully transfer the supernatant into a new 600 μL microcentrifuge tube.
Add 1/10 volume (10 μL) of 3 M sodium acetate solution (pH = 5.2).
Add an equal volume (110 μL) of isopropanol and 1 μL glycogen into the tube.
Pipette to mix thoroughly.
Incubate for precipitation about 12–16 hours at −20°C.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant but do not disturb the mRNA pellet.
Wash once with 220 μL of 80% ethanol and centrifuge at 16,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant again.
Air dry the RNA pellet for 5 minutes at 20°C–30°C.
Dissolve the RNA pellet with 10–20 μL of RNase-free water.
Mix 80 ng of a6A-enriched RNA with RNase-free water to a final volume of 26 μL.
Prepare iodination solution and add 4 μL to the RNA mixture, mixing well.
Incubate the brown-colored solution at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Transfer the incubated solution into a new tube.
Add sodium thiosulfate solution (0.2 M) drop by drop until the solution turns colorless and clear.
Add 6 μL sodium carbonate solution (pH = 9.5) to the reaction mixture.
Pipette to mix thoroughly.
Incubate at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Transfer the reaction mixture into a 600 μL microcentrifuge tube.
Add an equal volume of isopropanol and 1 μL glycogen.
Mix by pipetting.
Incubate for precipitation at -20°C for 12–16 hours.
Centrifuge at 16,000×g for 45 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant without disturbing the mRNA pellet.
Wash once with 80 μL of 80% ethanol.
Centrifuge again at 16,000×g for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Air dry the RNA pellet for 5 minutes at 20–30°C.
Dissolve the cycA-containing RNA pellet with 10 μL of RNase-free water.
Use the dissolved RNA directly or store it at -80°C.
Transfer RNA samples (10–50 ng) into new PCR tubes.
Prime the RNA samples following the protocol.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting up and down several times.
Briefly spin down the mixture.
Incubate the sample in a preheated thermal cycler at 65°C for 5 min.
Reduce temperature to 4°C with lid setting to 105°C.
Mix reagents in the tube for synthesizing first strand cDNA as indicated below.
Thoroughly mix by pipetting up and down several times.
Incubate the sample in a preheated thermal cycler with the heated lid set at ≥ 100°C.
Follow the protocol for Second Strand cDNA Synthesis and other continuing steps to complete the library construction.
Analyze all libraries with Agilent 2100 bioanalyzer.
Sequence libraries by Hiseq X10 in paired-end mode with read length of 150 bp using listed primers.
Quality control raw data with FastQC (version: v0.11.8) using command fastqc *gz -o ./fastqc/ -t 8.

Trim adapters from clean data by fastp (version: 0.19.7) using command fastp -x --detect_adapter_for_pe -l 25 -i R1.fastq.gz -I R2.fastq.gz -o ./fastp/R1.trim.fastq.gz -O ./fastp/R2.trim.fastq.gz -h fastp.html -j fastp.json.

Map clean data to corresponding genomes (hg38 for human and mm10 for mouse) with HISAT2 (version: 2.1.0) using command hisat2 -x index_flie_path/index -p 10 --rna-strandness RF --no-unal --no-mixed --no-discordant -t -1 R1.trim.fastq.gz -2 R2.trim.fastq.gz -S sample.sam --summary-file sample-align-summary.
Extract unique mapped data by samtools (version: 1.9) using command samtools view -S -h -q 30 -f 2 sample.sam > sample.unique.sam.
Convert and sort unique mapped Sam files into bam files by Samtools using command samtools sort -@ 4 sample_unique.sam -o sample_unique.bam.
Use exomePeak for peak calling.
Use samtools for mutation calling.
Execute the command: samtools mpileup -BQ0 -d 10000000 -o output.pileup.xls -f ref.fa sample.bam.
